# Memory Semiconductors (DRAM and NAND) — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global memory semiconductor manufacturers across 8 research dimensions. Report all currency in USD billions at FY-average FX, all bit shipments in EB, and all capex in USD-bn unless otherwise stated.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Samsung Electronics | 005930.KS |
| 2 | SK hynix | 000660.KS |
| 3 | Micron Technology | MU |
| 4 | Kioxia Holdings | 285A.T |
| 5 | Sandisk | SNDK |
| 6 | YMTC (Yangtze Memory Technologies) | Private |
| 7 | CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies) | Private |
| 8 | Nanya Technology | 2408.TW |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Revenue Decomposition — Memory vs Non-Memory**
For each entity, retrieve FY2025 (or latest reported full year) total revenue in USD billions, then decompose into memory-only versus non-memory contribution. For Samsung specifically, isolate DS-Memory from System LSI and Foundry, eliminating any inter-segment transfers. For private firms (YMTC, CXMT), triangulate across TrendForce, Omdia, and SemiAnalysis estimates and state which source you used and why. Memory and non-memory components must sum to consolidated revenue.

**Q2. DRAM:NAND Mix and ASP Ratio**
Compute each firm's DRAM:NAND revenue ratio for the most recent reported quarter, and separately compute the implied ASP (revenue ÷ bit shipments, USD/GB equivalent) for DRAM and NAND where bit data is disclosed. Rank the 8 firms by NAND-mix exposure to the 2025–26 enterprise SSD upcycle. Flag NAND-only (Kioxia, Sandisk, YMTC) and DRAM-only (CXMT, Nanya) entities explicitly.

**Q3. Market Share Reconciliation**
Retrieve TrendForce or Omdia reported quarterly DRAM and/or NAND market share (%) for the most recent quarter available, then reconcile against each firm's disclosed memory revenue divided by the implied DRAM/NAND TAM for that quarter. Identify any firm where the reconciled share gap exceeds 100 bps and state the most likely cause (pricing premium, product mix, accounting period mismatch). Cite source and reporting period.

**Q4. Node/Layer Vintage and Generation Lag**
For each firm, identify the most advanced DRAM node (1a/1b/1c/1d/1γ nm) and/or NAND layer count (232L / 238L / 286L / 321L+) currently in mass production, and state the calendar quarter of mass-production crossover. Compute the node-generation lag (in quarters) versus the leader for each of DRAM and NAND. Cite the source (press release, earnings call, or analyst report).

**Q5. HBM Position Score**
For each firm, score HBM competitive position on a 0–5 rubric combining (a) highest qualified generation (HBM3 / HBM3E / HBM4), (b) NVIDIA and/or AMD qualification status, (c) 12-Hi vs 16-Hi capability, (d) 2026 capacity-share guidance. State the weights you assigned to each sub-component. Explicitly mark firms that do not produce HBM as 0 with rationale.

**Q6. Memory Operating Margin YoY Bridge**
For each firm's most recent reported quarter, isolate the memory-segment operating margin (%) — for Samsung use DS-Memory, for Sandisk use post-spin standalone reporting. Bridge the YoY margin delta into four components: price, bit-growth, cost-down, and HBM-mix. The four components must sum to total YoY margin change. State HBM-mix contribution explicitly where disclosed; mark "n/a" for non-HBM producers.

**Q7. Capex Intensity and Bit-Growth Efficiency**
Retrieve FY2025 actual or FY2026 guided capex in USD billions; for Samsung isolate the memory portion of DS capex. Compute (i) capex/revenue intensity (%) and (ii) capex per EB of combined DRAM + NAND bit growth. Rank the 8 firms versus the median on both metrics; identify over- and under-investors and state the implied 2027 supply impact (tight / balanced / oversupplied) by product.

**Q8. Headquarters and Primary Fab Locations**
List each entity's headquarters (country/city) and primary manufacturing fab locations (country, city, site name, and DRAM/NAND designation). For each fab, state whether it is currently subject to US export controls or entity-list restrictions as of the latest available disclosure. Use SEMI World Fab Forecast or equivalent fab database alongside corporate disclosures.

### Narrative

**Samsung — DS-Memory isolation (the only material decomposition challenge among publics).** Samsung's Device Solutions (DS) division consolidates Memory, System LSI, and Foundry. The FY2025 Business Report Note on Operating Segments breaks DS revenue (~₩115T / ~$83B) into Memory ₩108T (~$78B), System LSI ₩24T (~$17B), and Foundry ₩26T (~$19B), with **negative ₩(43)T inter-segment eliminations** primarily from (i) Foundry wafers consumed by System LSI for Exynos/ISOCELL, and (ii) Memory die sold to DX (Mobile, VD/DA) for in-house use. After elimination, external DS-Memory revenue is ~$78B (range $74–82B reflecting ASP volatility in 2H25 NAND and the ₩/$ spot drift). DX (Mobile/VD/DA), Display (SDC), and Harman together account for the remaining ~$148B.

**SK hynix — near-pure-play.** SK hynix reports a single semiconductor segment in its consolidated annual report; the residual ~$1.3B non-memory revenue comprises CIS (CMOS Image Sensors) sold under "SK hynix system IC" and a small foundry-toll book in the Wuxi/Cheongju 8" line. HBM3E was the dominant FY25 growth vector; product-mix supplemental disclosure (deck slide 6, Q4'25) was used to carve out non-memory.

**Micron — effectively pure memory.** Micron's 10-K (FY25 ended 28-Aug-2025) reports four BUs (Compute & Networking, Mobile, Storage, Embedded) — all DRAM/NAND. The "other" line (~$0.4B, ~1%) per F-7 includes legacy services and is immaterial to the memory/non-memory split.

**Kioxia / Sandisk / Nanya — single-product entities.** All three report effectively 100% memory: Kioxia and Sandisk are NAND-only (raw + SSD modules treated as memory revenue); Nanya is DRAM-only. Sandisk's FY-25 figure is partially pre-spin (post-Feb-2025 standalone reporting only); CY2025 figure reconstructed from S-1/Form 10 carve-out + post-spin 10-Qs.

**Private-firm triangulation (YMTC, CXMT) — explicit methodology.** Neither firm publishes audited financials. I triangulated across three independent third-party trackers:

- **YMTC:** TrendForce 4Q25 NAND ranking ($1.5B Q4 → ~$5.8B FY annualized using their quarterly series), Omdia ($6.4B FY25 — higher because Omdia includes intra-group ZhiTai-branded module sales as separate revenue), SemiAnalysis ($5.0B — lower, adjusts for entity-list inventory drawdown that did not represent fresh production). **Adopted TrendForce midpoint $5.8B** because it is the most quoted in sell-side memory models and uses bit-shipment × ASP build-up which is methodologically transparent.

- **CXMT:** TrendForce $5.5B, Omdia $7.1B, SemiAnalysis $6.2B. **Adopted SemiAnalysis $6.2B** as primary because it uniquely adjusts for (a) DDR4-heavy product mix at ~30% ASP discount to global blended DRAM ASP, and (b) domestic-channel rebates not visible to TrendForce shipment trackers. Reported as point estimate $6.2B with interval [$4.8B–$7.5B].

### Cross-check: Memory + Non-Memory = Consolidated
All 8 rows sum exactly (Samsung: 78.0 + 148.0 = 226.0 ✓; SK hynix: 67.2 + 1.3 = 68.5 ✓; Micron: 36.4 + 0.4 = 36.8 ✓; remaining 5 are 100% memory by construction).

## Q2. DRAM:NAND Mix and ASP Ratio — Reference Answers

**Reporting period convention.** "Most recent reported quarter" as of 2026-04-30 = Calendar Q1 2026 (CQ1'26) for Samsung, SK hynix, and Nanya; Micron FQ2'26 (Dec'25–Feb'26); Kioxia FQ4'26 (Jan–Mar'26); Sandisk FQ3'26 (Jan–Mar'26). YMTC/CXMT are private — bit/revenue split triangulated from TrendForce *NAND/DRAM Industry Quarterly* and Omdia *Memory Market Tracker* 1Q26 release.

**ASP method.** Implied ASP (USD/GB) = product-line revenue ÷ bit shipments converted to GB (1 EB = 1.074×10⁹ GB). Where bit shipments are disclosed only in QoQ % terms, we anchor to the prior quarter's disclosed absolute level (Samsung 4Q24 IR appendix; SK hynix 4Q23 last-disclosed absolute) and roll forward — flagged as "rolled" tier-2 in the source column.

**Source tier legend.** T1 = audited filing / earnings release; T2 = company IR deck / earnings call transcript; T3 = TrendForce / Omdia / SemiAnalysis estimate; T4 = analyst triangulation.

### Narrative

**Mix observations.** DRAM:NAND revenue ratios span the full range, from 0:100 at the three pure-play NAND vendors (Kioxia, Sandisk, YMTC) to 100:0 at the two pure-play DRAM vendors (CXMT, Nanya). Among integrated players, **SK hynix is the most DRAM-skewed (~81:19)**, reflecting the HBM revenue mix premium and the structural decision to keep Solidigm reported but operationally separate. **Samsung sits at ~72:28**, the most balanced integrated portfolio, while **Micron is in between at ~76:24** following a deliberate FY25–26 wafer reallocation toward HBM3E/HBM4 and away from client NAND.

**ASP commentary.** Implied DRAM ASPs diverge sharply because HBM stacks are accounted for as DRAM revenue: SK hynix's blended ~$6.85/GB is roughly 2× the commodity DDR4 line of CXMT/Nanya (~$3.05–3.20/GB). This is *not* a like-for-like comparison — it reflects mix rather than pricing power on a node-equivalent basis. NAND ASPs cluster between $0.058 (YMTC, China-domestic-skewed) and $0.090 (Sandisk, channel/retail-skewed); enterprise-SSD-heavy vendors (SK hynix/Solidigm, Micron) sit mid-pack on blended NAND ASP because eSSD margin lifts blended pricing only modestly at the bit level.

**NAND-mix exposure ranking to the 2025–26 enterprise-SSD upcycle.** Pure NAND-mix is necessary but not sufficient — exposure is weighted by the *enterprise-SSD share within NAND*. Ranking (1 = most exposed):

1. **Sandisk** — 100% NAND but client/retail-skewed; reranked below pure eSSD plays. *Note: ranking adjusted — see footnote.*
2. **Kioxia** — 100% NAND with ~35–40% eSSD/datacenter mix and BiCS8 ramp tied to NVIDIA/hyperscaler qualifications.
3. **YMTC** — 100% NAND but constrained to China datacenter customers under entity-list restrictions; high domestic eSSD exposure within that boundary.
4. **Solidigm (within SK hynix)** — eSSD-pure; if treated standalone would be #1.
5. **Samsung** — 28% NAND of memory, but V8/V9 eSSD with hyperscaler qualifications dominates that mix.
6. **Micron** — 24% NAND with G8/G9 ramping into eSSD; lower absolute NAND base.
7. **SK hynix consolidated** — 19% NAND but ~60%+ of NAND is Solidigm eSSD → high quality of exposure despite low share.
8. **CXMT, Nanya (tied)** — 0% NAND, no direct exposure.

*Footnote on Sandisk:* Although Sandisk is NAND-only by mix, its post-spin reporting (Feb 2025 separation from Western Digital) shows ~70% client/retail/embedded and only ~20–25% eSSD/datacenter; consequently it is the lowest-quality 100%-NAND exposure among the three NAND pure-plays, and we placed it #1 by *raw mix* but it would drop to #5 on a quality-weighted basis. Both rankings are presented for transparency.

**ND-acceptable handling.** Bit shipments for Samsung's NAND line and SK hynix's NAND line are disclosed only as QoQ deltas in the 1Q26 calls; absolute bit levels are rolled forward from 4Q23 (SK hynix) and 4Q24 (Samsung) baselines using cumulative disclosed deltas. This introduces ±8% cumulative drift in the implied-ASP estimate, captured in the brackets above. YMTC and CXMT bit shipments are not disclosed at all — used TrendForce 1Q26 vendor-level wafer-out × disclosed average die density × yield assumption (90% DRAM / 85% NAND); cross-checked against Omdia. SemiAnalysis was preferred over Omdia for CXMT because its bottom-up DDR4/DDR5 mix split is more granular for 2026.

1. **SK hynix DRAM (−470 bps) and NAND (−120 bps).** This is the largest reconciled gap and is *not* a disclosure error. TrendForce's DRAM revenue table reports **HBM stack-level revenue** (i.e., the value of the assembled HBM cube sold to NVIDIA/AMD), whereas SK hynix's segmental disclosure books HBM at the **DRAM die transfer price** into its packaging operation. The ~USD 1.6 bn delta is the HBM TSV/assembly value-add. Re-grossing SK hynix DRAM revenue by the HBM stack uplift closes the gap to **~+50 bps**, confirming the reconciliation. The 120-bp NAND gap is driven by **Solidigm intercompany consolidation timing** (Solidigm reports on a one-month lag inside SK hynix's Korean GAAP). *Cause classification: pricing premium + accounting-period mismatch.*

2. **Micron NAND (−120 bps).** Driven purely by **fiscal-period mismatch**: Micron's F2Q26 ends 27-Feb-2026, capturing two months of soft Jan-Feb 2026 NAND contract pricing (ASP −5% MoM per DRAMeXchange). Calendarising to a strict Oct–Dec 2025 window using Micron's monthly bit-shipment color from the F2Q26 earnings call (5-Mar-2026, prepared remarks p.6) closes the gap to **−20 bps**. *Cause classification: accounting-period mismatch.*

All other firms reconcile within ±100 bps, which is below TrendForce's stated own ±150 bps methodological uncertainty (TrendForce *DRAM Revenue Methodology Note*, Jan-2024).

### Narrative — methodology, attribution, and uncertainty

Residual unexplained margin (FX, NRV reversal, one-offs) is folded into Cost-down to enforce the additive identity.

**Median (n=8):** Capex/Rev ≈ **27.0%**; Capex/EB ≈ **0.157 USD bn/EB**.

### Methodology notes

- **Samsung memory isolation:** Samsung does not split DS capex between Memory, System LSI, and Foundry in the audited statements. We use the FY2025 audit report's ₩47.5T DS-segment PP&E additions and apply the 67/33 memory:logic capex split disclosed by the CFO on the Q3'25 earnings call (28-Oct-2025), giving ₩31.8T ≈ USD 23.3bn. Range [22.0–25.0] reflects ±5pp uncertainty on the split.
- **Bit-growth Δ EB:** Computed as FY2025 shipped bits minus FY2024 shipped bits, using each firm's disclosed bit-shipment growth rates (Samsung: "high-teens" DRAM, "mid-30s%" NAND; SK hynix: "low-20s" DRAM, "30%+" NAND; Micron: per 10-K Item 7) applied to a base derived from TrendForce/Omdia FY2024 share × industry EB. For private firms, base bits are SemiAnalysis FY2024 estimates rolled forward.
- **ND-acceptable handling (YMTC/CXMT):** No audited financials. We disclose source preference (SemiAnalysis tool-tracker for YMTC; TrendForce + Hefei bond filings for CXMT) and provide ±25–30% intervals. Capex/Rev ratios >100% reflect that revenue is suppressed by sanctions/yield issues while capex continues via state financing — this is a *real* economic feature, not a measurement artifact.
- **Sandisk stub-year:** Spin completed Feb-2025; FY2025 capex is 11-month stub ($1.92bn) annualized to $2.10bn. Flash Ventures JV: only 50% of total tool spend hits Sandisk P&L, the other 50% hits Kioxia — this is why both firms appear capital-light per disclosed capex.
- **Nanya outlier:** Capex/Rev = 90% reflects the multi-year 10nm-class (1B-nm) capacity build at Fab-3B (Hwaya) while revenue remains depressed by DDR4 ASP weakness. Capex/EB = 0.297 is the worst in the cohort (excluding China-state firms) but mostly reflects the *front-loaded* nature of a single-fab operator.

### Ranking and over/under-investor calls

**Over-investors (Capex/Rev > median + 5pp AND Capex/EB > median):**
1. **CXMT** (226% / 0.250) — implies **DDR4/LPDDR4 oversupply by 2H-2027** in domestic-China commodity DRAM; mainstream DDR5 stays balanced as CXMT yield ramps.
2. **Nanya** (90.5% / 0.297) — but small absolute scale (~3% global DRAM); negligible global-supply impact.
3. **YMTC** (111% / 0.214) — capacity additions concentrated in domestic-China NAND; **ex-China NAND market unaffected**, domestic balanced-to-oversupplied.
4. **Micron** (42.6% / 0.173) — heavy but *intentional* HBM/Idaho greenfield; supports HBM-driven DRAM tightness through 2027.

**Under-investors (Capex/Rev ≤ median AND Capex/EB ≤ median):**
1. **Samsung DS-Memory** (26.7% / 0.105) — most efficient absolute bit-add per dollar, reflecting depreciated mega-fab base and HBM3E ramp from existing 1b-nm capacity.
2. **SK hynix** (26.4% / 0.110) — efficient despite HBM mix because TSV uplift comes off existing 1a/1b wafers; M15X ramp pushes FY26 capex up >20%.
3. **Kioxia** (27.3% / 0.051) — efficient via Yokkaichi/Kitakami JV scale.
4. **Sandisk** (26.9% / 0.034) — capital-light by JV-accounting design.

### 2027 Supply Implication (by product)

- **HBM (premium DRAM):** **Tight** — capacity is gated by TSV/advanced-packaging tools (Samsung, SK hynix, Micron triopoly), not by wafer capex.
- **Mainstream DDR5/LPDDR5X:** **Balanced** — incumbent capex disciplined; CXMT not yet qualified at hyperscalers.
- **Commodity DDR4/LPDDR4:** **Oversupplied** — CXMT + Nanya bit-adds exceed legacy demand decay.
- **Enterprise NAND (TLC/QLC):** **Balanced-to-tight** — Kioxia/Sandisk/Samsung capex measured; SemiAnalysis projects 2027 NAND bit-supply CAGR ~28% vs demand 30%+.
- **Consumer NAND:** **Balanced** — YMTC domestic absorption offsets ex-China discipline.

### Source-tier legend

- **T1** = audited financial statements (10-K, 20-F, 有価証券報告書, KOSPI annual report, TWSE annual report)
- **T2** = earnings-call transcripts, investor-day decks, official press releases
- **T3** = TrendForce / Omdia / SemiAnalysis subscription research
- **T4** = trade press, customs/bond-prospectus disclosures

Cells flagged "ND" (YMTC, CXMT) rely on T3 with T4 corroboration; intervals reflect ±25–30% standard error on private-firm capex estimates per SemiAnalysis methodology disclosure (Mar-2026).

The geography of memory production remains highly concentrated: **~70% of global DRAM wafer capacity sits in South Korea (Samsung + SK hynix)**, with Taiwan (Micron Taichung/Taoyuan + Nanya) as the secondary cluster, and CXMT as the rising mainland-China DRAM node. **NAND is bifurcated** between Korean (Samsung Pyeongtaek/Xi'an, SK hynix Cheongju/Dalian), Japanese (Kioxia & Sandisk JV at Yokkaichi/Kitakami), Singapore (Micron Fab 10), and Wuhan (YMTC).

**Export-control exposure** is the discriminating axis: only **YMTC sits on the BIS Entity List** (Dec-2022), preventing it from procuring US-origin SME for ≥128L production without a license — a binding constraint reflected in delayed 232L+ ramp. **Samsung Xi'an and SK hynix Wuxi/Dalian** were carved out via **indefinite VEU authorizations** in October 2023, allowing continued (though capped) advanced-node operation. **CXMT** itself remains off the Entity List as of this report date, but operates under the Oct-2022/2023 sub-18 nm DRAM SME embargo and saw affiliated subsidiaries (SwaySure, PXW) added Dec-2024; consensus among SemiAnalysis and TrendForce is that direct CXMT designation is a non-trivial 2026 risk.

## Q1. Revenue Decomposition

## Q2. DRAM:NAND Mix And ASP

No inspected public release disclosed absolute DRAM/NAND bit shipments in EB by company, so true revenue ÷ EB ASP cannot be computed from disclosures alone. ASP/GB below is therefore marked “not disclosed” unless only directional ASP/bit-growth was disclosed.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|

NAND exposure ranking for the enterprise SSD upcycle: `Kioxia = Sandisk = YMTC` highest at 100%, then `Samsung`, `SK hynix`, `Micron`, then `CXMT = Nanya` at 0%.

## Q3. Market Share Reconciliation

TrendForce reported 3Q25 DRAM industry revenue of $41.4B, up 30.9% QoQ. Public accessible TrendForce data gives Samsung and SK hynix shares for 2Q25 and confirms Micron gained 3.7 percentage points in 3Q25; detailed 3Q25 vendor table was not fully accessible, so the reconciliation uses inferred 3Q25 shares.

## Q6. Memory Operating Margin YoY Bridge

Where segment margin was not disclosed, this is a model bridge. Components sum to the stated delta; HBM mix is `n/a` for non-HBM producers.

## Q7. Capex Intensity And Bit-Growth Efficiency

Capex and EB growth are partly modelled because company-level DRAM/NAND EB shipments are generally not disclosed.

## Q2. DRAM:NAND Mix and ASP Ratio (4Q25 / latest reported quarter)

Q4.rationale: Several node/layer calls are directionally plausible, especially SK hynix and the Kioxia/Sandisk BiCS8 linkage, but crossover quarters and most-advanced generations are often wrong. Q5.rationale: Weights are stated and non-HBM producers are mostly marked zero with rationale, but Samsung is over-scored and Micron/SK share or qualification details are inaccurate. CXMT receives partial credit for recognizing small optionality, but the sourcing and generation details are weak.

Q6.rationale: The margin bridges use wrong quarters and largely incorrect operating margins, with Samsung/SK hynix/Micron overstated dramatically. Most non-HBM producers lack the required quantified four-component bridge, and private-company methods are not disclosed.

Q7.rationale: Capex values and median comparisons are often wrong or qualitative, with SK hynix especially far off. Capex per EB is generally not computed, Samsung memory capex is under-isolated, and private-firm ND methods are inadequate.

Q8.rationale: Most HQs and major fab geographies are directionally correct, but restriction status is often imprecise, especially Samsung/SK hynix VEU treatment. Nanya's HQ and fab locations are materially wrong, and several entries include non-memory or speculative sites.

Q1.rationale: Several public-company totals are directionally close, but many decompositions miss required carve-outs, fiscal conventions, or private-company triangulation. YMTC, CXMT, and Nanya are materially wrong versus reference ranges.

Q2.rationale: The answer uses the wrong period and NAND ASPs are off by roughly an order of magnitude for most producers. CXMT and Nanya get partial credit for correctly identifying DRAM-only status and plausible DRAM ASPs.

Q3.rationale: The TAM anchors are materially wrong and the key SK hynix HBM stack-vs-die accounting trap is missed entirely. Some NAND share cells are directionally close, but reconciliation detail and private-firm methods are weak.

Q4.rationale: The response uses the wrong DRAM leader anchor by naming Micron as leader, which breaks the lag framework. Some node/layer names are directionally recognizable, but crossover quarters and lag calculations are often wrong.

Q5.rationale: The answer states weights and correctly recognizes most non-HBM producers as zero, but Samsung and Micron/SK scores deviate from the reference rubric and several HBM qualification claims are overstated. CXMT loses credit for being scored flat zero without acknowledging HBM2 optionality.

Q6.rationale: The answer uses the wrong quarter and reported margins are largely incompatible with the reference, including severe errors for Samsung, SK hynix, and Nanya. Private firms are left as not disclosed despite the rubric requiring estimates.

Q7.rationale: Most capex values, capex/revenue intensities, and capex/EB efficiencies are far from the reference. Required median benchmarking, Samsung memory capex isolation, private-company intervals, and Sandisk JV accounting are largely mishandled.

Q8.rationale: Several headquarters and broad fab geographies are directionally right, but restriction status is materially wrong for Samsung/SK VEU and CXMT. Fab completeness and product tags are also incomplete for Micron, Nanya, and the private entities.

## Q7. Capex Intensity and Bit-Growth Efficiency

### Summary Caveats

1. **Currency conversion** uses FY-average estimated rates; actual quarterly rates vary.
2. **Private firms** (YMTC, CXMT) rely on analyst estimates and industry triangulation — financial data is not audited public disclosure.
3. **Margin bridges** in Q6 are partially derived estimates where firms do not explicitly break out YoY drivers into the four requested components.
4. **Node generations** are based on company announcements and industry reports; "mass production crossover" dates are best estimates.
5. **Capex figures** for private firms and for Samsung's memory-only portion are estimated using industry analyst data.
6. **All data current as of latest available reports through May 2026.**

Q1.rationale: Several public-company totals are directionally close, but key carve-outs, fiscal conventions, and citations are incomplete. CXMT and Nanya are materially wrong, and private-firm triangulation is weak.

Q2.rationale: The answer usually identifies DRAM-only/NAND-only direction, but it largely omits required numeric ASPs and uses the wrong reporting period. Rankings are qualitative and several are materially off.

Q3.rationale: The reconciliation uses incorrect TAMs and misses the main SK hynix HBM accounting trap. Private entities are not properly triangulated, and several reported/implied shares are materially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Some leading-edge node/layer labels are directionally correct, but crossover quarters, lag calculations, and MP-versus-sampling distinctions are often wrong or vague. Private-firm ND handling is insufficient.

Q5.rationale: Weights are stated and non-HBM producers mostly get zero, but Samsung and Micron scores are materially wrong with unsupported HBM4 claims. CXMT is scored flat zero without acknowledging the small HBM2 optionality required by the reference.

Q6.rationale: The answer uses mostly wrong quarters and margins, with large deviations from the required Q1/FQ comparisons. Private-firm bridges are missing and several components do not meet the required bridge methodology.

Q7.rationale: Capex figures are often rough and capex-per-EB efficiency is essentially omitted. Median benchmarking is wrong, Sandisk is off by an order of magnitude, and private-firm estimates lack required intervals and source-preference rationale.

Q8.rationale: Major locations are partially captured, but restriction statuses are often wrong or incomplete, especially VEU treatment and CXMT. Sandisk JV structure is partly correct, while YMTC/CXMT private-fab triangulation is not adequately handled.

**Implied ASP** (revenue ÷ bit shipments) cannot be reliably computed for most firms because bit-shipment volumes are not publicly disclosed at the granular per-firm level for the most recent quarter. Q1.rationale: Several public-company totals are directionally plausible, but many miss required decomposition details, fiscal conventions, or private-firm triangulation. Nanya is materially wrong and Samsung lacks the required precise DS-Memory/System LSI/Foundry reconciliation.

Q2.rationale: The answer mostly gives only directional DRAM:NAND mix and flags pure-play entities, but omits the required ASP calculations and uses the wrong/latest periods for multiple firms. NAND exposure ranking is raw-mix only and lacks the required quality-weighted enterprise SSD treatment.

Q3.rationale: The reconciliation uses materially wrong TAMs and shares, misses the key SK hynix HBM stack-vs-die accounting mechanism, and omits private-firm reconciliations. Kioxia, Sandisk, and Nanya receive only minimal credit for directional share discussion.

Q4.rationale: The leader framing is roughly right, but many node/layer labels and crossover quarters are wrong or vague. Kioxia and Sandisk get partial credit for correctly identifying BiCS8/218L and NAND-only status.
